items.title: Qualify Arcadia authoring with a seeded workbook
preconditions: This is an authoring qualification input, not collected evidence, a coverage decision, an approval or a validation receipt.
Use the qualified AAD enterprise session and a test-owned disposable blank workbook.
Select Arcadia and verify the actual visible experience before executing the scenario.
Reuse the existing workbook seed and protected exact-value assertion providers; any missing registration is an external owning-workflow prerequisite, not permission to edit the harness.
After authoring, require five consecutive real local passes on the final implementation SHA with workers=1 and retries=0. Any implementation edit resets this case's counter.
orderedTestSteps: Create and open the test-owned disposable workbook through the existing AAD Hub flow.
Seed A1 with the exact value 5 and read it back using the existing protected workbook reader.
Open the Excel Agent pane and confirm Arcadia.
Send the exact prompt: Read the number currently in A1, add 10, and write the result back into A1.
Wait for the edit to finish and read A1 through the protected workbook verifier.
expectedUserVisibleAndDataOutcomes: The initial workbook A1 value is exactly 5.
The final workbook A1 value is exactly 15, read from the real workbook rather than inferred from the chat response.
The scenario actually executes in Arcadia; an unavailable session, wrong experience, unreadable cell or skipped test is not a pass.
cleanup: Close only the browser context or tab owned by this test, including when setup or an assertion fails.
Do not overwrite or delete any pre-existing workbook or user-owned page.

items.title: Qualify MSA authoring with conversation isolation
preconditions: Use the approved consumer MSA login harness; never substitute an AAD session or treat an authentication skip as success.
Open a test-owned disposable workbook, select Omni, and verify the actual experience.
Reuse the existing exact-canary conversation and workbook-unchanged assertion contracts without adding generic generated-prose matching.
After authoring, require five consecutive real local passes on the final implementation SHA with workers=1 and retries=0. Any implementation edit resets this case's counter.
orderedTestSteps: Open the consumer MSA Excel Agent pane in the test-owned workbook and confirm Omni and the consumer account lane.
Seed A1 with the sentinel FIXTURE_WORKBOOK_UNCHANGED and read it back.
Start a new conversation and ask the agent to remember the exact token QUALIFY-1JS-MSA-7D31A9 without writing it to the workbook.
In a second turn ask for the remembered token without including it in that second prompt.
Start New Chat, confirm the previous messages are gone, and ask for the previous conversation's remembered token without including it in the prompt.
Read A1 again with the protected workbook verifier.
expectedUserVisibleAndDataOutcomes: The second turn in the original conversation contains the exact token QUALIFY-1JS-MSA-7D31A9.
The completed reply after New Chat must not contain QUALIFY-1JS-MSA-7D31A9.
The test uses the consumer MSA lane and Omni throughout; missing credentials, skipped execution or a substituted enterprise account is not a pass.
cleanup: Close only the browser context or tab owned by this test, even if login, conversation or workbook verification fails.
Do not close or sign out any pre-existing consumer session.

items.title: Qualify generated state mutation and restoration
preconditions: Use the qualified AAD enterprise account, the actual Omni experience and a test-owned disposable workbook.
Execute serially with every case sharing this profile or mutable account setting.
Reuse the existing source toggle, persisted-state assertion and paired restoration contracts; capture the original value before the first mutation.
After authoring, require five consecutive real local passes on the final implementation SHA with workers=1 and retries=0. Any implementation edit resets this case's counter.
orderedTestSteps: Open the Excel Agent pane and confirm the Omni experience and AAD account lane.
Open the source picker and record the current Web source value.
Enable Web while capturing the original value, then disable Web using existing declarative state-saving operations.
Close and reopen the picker and assert the disabled value persists.
Finish the scenario through the existing paired cleanup operation.
expectedUserVisibleAndDataOutcomes: Web is enabled and then disabled, exercising an actual state change regardless of its initial value.
After cleanup, reopening the picker shows the exact original value, irrespective of whether it was initially enabled or disabled.
The next execution starts without inheriting a changed setting from the preceding execution.
cleanup: Restore the exact original Web source value even if an intermediate step or assertion fails; report restoration failure explicitly.
Close only the browser context or tab owned by this test after restoration is attempted.
Preserve every pre-existing page and other account setting.

items.title: Qualify a local file fixture combined with workbook data
preconditions: Use the qualified AAD enterprise session, actual Arcadia experience and a test-owned disposable workbook.
Use the registered ingestion-source CSV, whose Engineering salaries sum to 2500; do not invent a resource provider or substitute chat-only evidence.
After authoring, require five consecutive real local passes on the final implementation SHA with workers=1 and retries=0. Any implementation edit resets this case's counter.
orderedTestSteps: Create a test-owned workbook and confirm Arcadia.
Seed H1 with exactly 100 and record its protected readback; seed E1 with a non-result sentinel.
Upload ingestion-source through the existing local-file upload composite and wait for its own completed attachment.
Ask the agent to total the uploaded file's Engineering salaries plus H1, writing only E1.
Read E1 and H1 through the protected workbook verifier.
expectedUserVisibleAndDataOutcomes: E1 is exactly 2600 in the real workbook.
H1 remains exactly 100 throughout the protected unchanged observation.
The completed attachment belongs to this upload; a restored or unrelated file is not success.
cleanup: Close only the browser context or tab owned by this test, including on upload or assertion failure.
Preserve the repository fixture file, pre-existing workbooks and user-owned pages.

items.title: Qualify an owned persistent custom-skill fixture
preconditions: Require the existing EXCELAGENT_CUSTOM_SKILL_E2E_ENABLED gate, verified matching principal and explicit SharePoint resource/cleanup authorization; otherwise report this case blocked.
Use the qualified AAD enterprise session, actual Arcadia experience and a test-owned disposable workbook.
Reuse the registered sample-custom-skill fixture and its unique per-run owned name; never fetch or save credentials or alter another skill.
After authoring, require five consecutive real local passes on the final implementation SHA with workers=1 and retries=0. Any implementation edit resets this case's counter.
orderedTestSteps: Seed A1 with a non-result sentinel and capture a protected neighboring-cell guard in B1.
Upload the uniquely named sample skill through the existing provider and capture its owned resource descriptor.
Select and invoke exactly that skill in Arcadia.
Read A1 and B1 using protected workbook assertions.
Close Manage Skills and remove exactly the captured owned skill through paired cleanup.
expectedUserVisibleAndDataOutcomes: A1 is exactly 314159 in the real workbook and B1 remains unchanged.
The newly uploaded skill is invoked by exact identity, not inferred from generated prose.
The owned skill is removed; removal failures are reported rather than treated as passes.
cleanup: Attempt removal of only the owned custom-skill resource even when invocation or workbook verification fails.
Close only the browser context or tab owned by this test after resource cleanup; preserve pre-existing pages and skills.

items.title: Qualify a dedicated enterprise account and named workbook fixture
preconditions: This AAD case specifically requires the dedicated-enterprise lane, not the ordinary AAD browser profile.
Require the approved ENTERPRISE_E2E_ENABLED gate, dedicated external-service login and existing clp-labeled named workbook; otherwise report this case blocked.
Never fetch or save credentials, invent a fixture URL, relabel the shared workbook or substitute an ordinary blank workbook.
After authoring, require five consecutive real local passes on the final implementation SHA with workers=1 and retries=0. Any implementation edit resets this case's counter.
orderedTestSteps: Resolve the approved clp-labeled workbook through the registered dedicated fixture provider.
Run the existing external-service login pre-session contract and confirm the dedicated account lane.
Open the workbook and confirm Arcadia.
Assert the actual sensitivity label is visible using the existing protected sensitivity provider.
expectedUserVisibleAndDataOutcomes: The dedicated named workbook's sensitivity label is visible.
The shared workbook is not mutated and its sensitivity is not changed.
An unavailable dedicated login or named resource is blocked, not skipped into a successful qualification.
cleanup: Close only the browser context or tab owned by this test, including when dedicated login or startup fails.
Preserve the shared named workbook, its label and every pre-existing user session.
